evidence_rule: A deficiency remains UNPROVEN until its required external or distributed observation exists; implemented code is not promoted into operational fact.

items.subject: Multi-host coordinate convergence under partition/rejoin
items.why_unproven: All executed coordinate-directory tests ran inside one Linux process environment using in-memory peers or local files. No two admitted physical hosts exchanged snapshots across an actual network partition and rejoin.
items.why_cause_unaddressed: The code exposes merge(snapshot) but there is no resident peer membership, authenticated coordinate-sync transport, anti-entropy scheduler or per-peer checkpoint service that would cause snapshots to move between machines.
items.why_concept_remains: Vector clocks and conflict resolution are meaningful distributed primitives only after independently evolving replicas exchange state. Local simulation proves algorithms, not network convergence.
missing_architecture: mTLS or equivalently authenticated peer transport
partition/rejoin fault harness across at least two hosts
failure detector and peer freshness model

items.subject: Crash-fault or Byzantine consensus
items.why_unproven: The directory detects concurrent histories but does not elect a leader, form a quorum, replicate an ordered log or decide a single value under failures.
items.why_cause_unaddressed: The requested layer was a non-consensus distributed coordinate directory and reconciler. No consensus protocol, quorum membership or replicated log has been introduced.
items.why_concept_remains: Conflict detection/resolution cannot substitute for consensus where a globally ordered authoritative decision is required.
missing_architecture: explicit decision whether crash-fault consensus is required
Raft/Paxos-style replicated log if crash faults are the target
BFT protocol only if Byzantine tolerance is actually required
per-node cryptographic identity if adversarial nodes are in scope

items.subject: Distributed durability and serialization
items.why_unproven: AtomicJsonStore uses local lock files, fsync, atomic rename and local directory fsync. Those operations do not serialize writers on different hosts and their guarantees depend on the backing filesystem.
items.why_cause_unaddressed: There is no distributed lock/lease service, fencing token service or replicated datastore under the control plane.
items.why_concept_remains: Two machines can independently believe they hold authority over different local copies unless a shared ordering/fencing architecture exists.
missing_architecture: replicated durable state store or consensus-backed metadata service

items.subject: Standards-based network management datastore and device actuation
items.why_unproven: Layer-2 uses a generic JavaScript adapter interface. No live router, switch, Linux network namespace, FRR daemon or appliance was changed and read back through a standardized management protocol.
items.why_cause_unaddressed: No NETCONF, RESTCONF, gNMI or direct FRR/Linux adapter is present in this event_runner layer, and there is no YANG/NMDA datastore service.
items.why_concept_remains: A reconciler without concrete actuators can prove controller semantics but cannot prove real network configuration convergence.
missing_architecture: YANG models for desired and operational Keddeh network state
live readback parsers and reconciliation receipts

items.subject: HTTP ingress cryptographic identity
items.why_unproven: The ingress uses an X-KEX-Secret shared secret and the dispatcher signs an internal event envelope with HMAC. It does not sign the received HTTP request according to RFC 9421.
items.why_cause_unaddressed: There is no HTTP Message Signatures implementation, Content-Digest binding, signer key registry, asymmetric identity or rotation protocol in this layer.
items.why_concept_remains: The internal HMAC establishes possession of a shared key after classification, but does not provide standards-based end-to-end integrity over selected HTTP message components.
missing_architecture: RFC 9421 signer/verifier or explicitly documented alternative
nonce/time policy integrated with durable replay journal
separation of ingress authentication key from event-signing key

items.subject: Canonical cryptographic JSON interoperability
items.why_unproven: Hashing uses recursively sorted JavaScript object keys plus JSON.stringify. This is deterministic for tested fixtures but is not a complete RFC 8785 JCS implementation.
items.why_cause_unaddressed: No JCS library or RFC conformance vectors are installed, and no I-JSON validation layer exists.
items.why_concept_remains: Cross-language hashing can diverge on number/string serialization edge cases even when ordinary fixtures match.
missing_architecture: cross-language hash compatibility suite for JavaScript/Python/Swift

items.subject: Loss recovery and full source resynchronization
items.why_unproven: The ToT journal now rejects a sequence gap after a baseline but does not itself fetch or reconstruct the missing source state.
items.why_cause_unaddressed: The Sheet emitter has no snapshot/resync endpoint and there is no subscriber checkpoint/resynchronization protocol between source, dispatcher and runner.
items.why_concept_remains: Detection prevents silent data loss, but a denied gap remains operationally blocked until authoritative state can be replayed or replaced with a full snapshot.
missing_architecture: checkpoint acknowledgement and safe sequence reset
idempotent replay log or source event journal

items.subject: Live GitHub Actions qualification and telemetry runner execution
items.why_unproven: Latest Report 03 workflow run 35583950905 completed failure with a qualify job but no executed steps; telemetry run 35583949510 returned no jobs. Therefore GitHub did not execute the application qualification path.
items.why_cause_unaddressed: The failure occurs before workflow steps, outside the tested event_runner code. No functioning GitHub-hosted qualification runner or admitted self-hosted kex/telemetry runner has been observed for these runs.
items.why_concept_remains: Repository code can be locally correct while the external job scheduler/runner plane remains unavailable.
missing_architecture: diagnosed GitHub Actions account/repository runner-allocation path
admitted healthy self-hosted runner for telemetry
ephemeral or JIT provisioning rather than persistent shared host
private or otherwise appropriately isolated repository/workflow trust boundary

items.subject: Self-hosted runner security on public repository
items.why_unproven: The repository is public and the telemetry workflow targets a self-hosted runner. GitHub currently warns that self-hosted runners should almost never be used for public repositories because untrusted workflow code can persistently compromise them.
items.why_cause_unaddressed: The repository/trust topology has not been changed and the installer still provisions a persistent service runner.
items.why_concept_remains: Runner-side ToT validates event payloads but cannot protect a host from arbitrary workflow code that executes before or alongside that validator if repository/workflow trust is compromised.
missing_architecture: private execution repository or strongly restricted runner-access topology

items.subject: Live Google Sheet trigger and ingress path
items.why_unproven: TelemetryDispatch.gs is repository code only. No observed installable trigger invocation, UrlFetch response, dispatcher receipt and downstream runner receipt have been captured from the real spreadsheet.
items.why_cause_unaddressed: Apps Script deployment, Script Properties, trigger binding and a reachable ingress endpoint are external operational bindings not executed in this qualification.
items.why_concept_remains: A correct Apps Script function cannot prove that Google invokes it, that credentials are configured, or that its endpoint is reachable.
missing_architecture: end-to-end correlation ID from Sheet to runner

items.subject: Physical host identity and attestation
items.why_unproven: authority_id and shared-key signatures identify a configured software authority, not the physical host, boot state, TPM identity or resident-root trust state.
items.why_cause_unaddressed: No hardware-backed attestation or observed BRAINK resident-root verification is integrated into this event path.
items.why_concept_remains: Possession of a secret does not establish that execution happened on the intended uncompromised machine.
missing_architecture: optional TPM/Secure Enclave attestation where required
mapping from runner identity to admitted BRAINK host

items.subject: Evidence immutability beyond one local filesystem
items.why_unproven: The JSONL ledger detects modification when an expected head is retained, but an attacker with full local filesystem control can rewrite the entire ledger and its local head.
items.why_cause_unaddressed: No external anchor, replicated witness, WORM store or transparency service receives the ledger head.
items.why_concept_remains: Hash chaining gives tamper evidence relative to a trusted prior root; it does not create an independent witness by itself.

items.subject: Production availability and recovery
items.why_unproven: Tests exercise faults inside one local runtime, not host loss, process restart storms, disk exhaustion, network latency/loss, dependency outage or failover across production hosts.
items.why_cause_unaddressed: No multi-host deployed service, SLO telemetry, failover topology or disaster-recovery environment is active in this evidence set.
items.why_concept_remains: Unit/fault-injection correctness is necessary but cannot measure availability or recovery objectives.
missing_architecture: RTO/RPO policy and measured recovery receipts
